---
title: "Viewing results"
---

SeekDeep has two local web viewers. Each one starts a small web server on your machine that you
open in a browser.

| Viewer | Reads | Use it for |
|---|---|---|
| [`pmoViewer`](../reference/seekdeepserver.qmd#pmoViewer) | A PMO file (`allPMO.json.gz` from elucidatornf, or any PMO) | elucidatornf results, and PMOs from other pipelines |
| [`popClusteringViewer`](../reference/seekdeepserver.qmd#popClusteringViewer) | A `processClusters` output directory | Running the SeekDeep commands yourself |

Both servers listen only on `127.0.0.1` (this machine) by default. To view results on a remote
machine, see [Viewing results on a server](#remote).

## pmoViewer

```bash
SeekDeep pmoViewer --pmo results/finalResults/allPMO.json.gz
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:9882/pmv>. The server runs until you stop it (Ctrl-C).

- `--port` changes the port (default `9882`), for example when it's already in use or you're
  serving several PMOs at once.
- `--name` changes the path at the end of the URL (default `pmv`).
- `--numThreads` speeds up comparing samples on the haplotype page.

## popClusteringViewer

`popClusteringViewer` serves one or more `processClusters` output directories. Each one is
described by a config file made with `genProjectConfig`, and the viewer serves every config file in
a directory:

```bash
mkdir configs
SeekDeep genProjectConfig --mainDir popClustering/ --projectName myProject --shortName myProject \
  --out configs/myProject.config
SeekDeep popClusteringViewer --configDir configs
```

Then open <http://127.0.0.1:9881/pcv>.

- `--mainDir` is the directory `processClusters` wrote.
- `--shortName` goes in the project's URL, so use only letters, numbers, `-` and `_`.
- Add more config files to `configs/` to serve several projects from one server.
- `--port` changes the port (default `9881`).

## Viewing results on a server {#remote}

Start the viewer on the server, then forward its port over SSH from your own machine and open the
same URL locally:

```bash
# on your own machine
ssh -N -L 9882:127.0.0.1:9882 you@server
```

To make the viewer reachable from other machines, give `--bindAddress 0.0.0.0`. It has no login,
so only do this on a network you trust.

With Docker, the viewer has to listen on all interfaces inside the container, and the port has to be
published:

```bash
docker run --rm -p 9882:9882 -v "$PWD":/data -w /data nickjhathaway/elucidator:develop \
  SeekDeep pmoViewer --pmo results/finalResults/allPMO.json.gz --bindAddress 0.0.0.0
```
